title: 1. The ball rolls downhill
q: Before the ball closes the switch, which statement best describes the energy change as it rolls down the ramp?
choices: Gravitational potential energy decreases, while the ball gains kinetic energy in its forward motion and rotation.
Gravitational potential energy increases because the ball is moving faster.
The ramp creates kinetic energy without any decrease in stored energy.
The battery transfers electrical energy to the ball while the switch is still open.
feedback: As the ball loses height, gravitational potential energy of the ball–Earth system decreases and kinetic energy increases. Rolling includes both forward motion and rotation. In a real device, some energy also transfers into thermal energy and sound; energy is not created by the ramp.

title: 2. The switch starts a different energy supply
q: The ball comes to rest in the switch cup, but the fan continues to push the sail cart. Which explanation best identifies the energy supply and transfers?
choices: The ball supplies all the fan’s energy, and the battery only controls when that energy is released.
The switch creates electrical energy, which the fan stores as gravitational potential energy.
The battery’s chemical energy supplies electrical energy to the motor; the fan moves air, which transfers energy to the cart.
The cart gains energy from the finish marker as it approaches it.
feedback: The ball triggers the switch. The battery provides a separate chemical energy store. Energy is transferred electrically to the motor and converted into the kinetic energy of the fan and moving air. Air pushes the sail and transfers energy to the cart. Some energy also becomes thermal energy and sound.

title: 3. The bucket falls and the flag rises
q: After the ball enters the bucket, the bucket-and-ball descend while the flag rises. Which account of energy is correct?
choices: The fixed pulley creates new gravitational potential energy as it turns.
The bucket-and-ball lose gravitational potential energy; energy transferred through the rope increases the flag’s gravitational potential energy.
The flag loses gravitational potential energy because the bucket is moving downward.
The falling bucket transforms gravitational potential energy into electrical energy inside the rope.
feedback: Include Earth when discussing gravitational potential energy. As the bucket-and-ball move downward, their gravitational potential energy decreases. The rope transfers energy to the rising flag, increasing its gravitational potential energy. The fixed pulley redirects the rope’s pull; it does not create energy. Moving parts can also have kinetic energy, and friction and impacts can transfer energy into thermal energy and sound.
